provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Being honest
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say what honesty means.
The pupils should be able to return lost items.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about good manners.
Today we will learn about being honest.
Content:
Honesty means saying the truth always.
If you find a toy that is not yours, return it.
Example: If you find a pencil in class, give it to the teacher.
Class activity:
Let's play a game called truth time.
I will ask questions and you must tell the truth.
Evaluation questions:
What does honesty mean?
What should you do if you find money?
Why is it good to be honest?
Summary:
Always tell the truth and return what is not yours.

topics.title: Being responsible
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list two responsibilities.
The pupils should be able to care for their belongings.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about being honest.
Today we will learn about being responsible.
Content:
Being responsible means doing your own jobs.
Keep your bag and bottle in the right place.
Example: Pack your bag yourself after school.
Class activity:
Let's practice packing our bags.
Put your bottle and book inside your bag.
Evaluation questions:
What does responsible mean?
What should you do with your bag?
Why is it important to do jobs yourself?
Summary:
Keep your things safe and do your own jobs.

topics.title: Respecting our flag and anthem
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to stand for the anthem.
The pupils should be able to handle the flag with care.
Introduction:
We love our country Nigeria.
Today we will learn how to respect our flag and anthem.
Content:
When we hear the national anthem, we stand still.
We do not play when the flag is being raised.
Example: During assembly, we stand quietly for the anthem.
Class activity:
Let's practice standing for the anthem.
When I play the music, stand up straight.
Evaluation questions:
What do we do during the national anthem?
How should we treat the Nigerian flag?
Why is it important to respect our symbols?
Summary:
Always stand for the anthem and respect our flag.

topics.title: Our community helpers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name community helpers.
The pupils should be able to say what each helper does.
Introduction:
In our community, many people help us.
Today we will learn about these helpers.
Content:
A teacher helps us learn in school.
A doctor helps us when we are sick.
A police officer keeps us safe.
Example: When you fall, the nurse helps you.
Class activity:
Let's pretend to be community helpers.
Who wants to be a doctor and help a friend?
Evaluation questions:
Name a community helper.
What does a teacher do?
Who helps us when we are sick?
Why are community helpers important?
Summary:
Community helpers are important and we should thank them.

topics.title: Kindness to animals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to feed animals gently.
The pupils should be able to say why we should not hurt animals.
Introduction:
We have many animals in Nigeria.
Today we will learn how to be kind to them.
Content:
We should feed animals like goats and dogs gently.
Do not throw stones at animals or pull their tails.
Example: When you see a stray dog, do not chase it away.
Class activity:
Let's pretend to feed a dog.
Take pretend food and give it to the dog gently.
Evaluation questions:
How should we feed animals?
Why should we not throw stones at animals?
What animals do you see in your community?
Summary:
Always be kind and gentle to all animals.

topics.title: Good behaviour outside
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use a quiet voice in public.
The pupils should be able to behave well in markets.
Introduction:\>Last week we learned about being kind to animals.
Today we will learn how to behave outside.
Content:
When we are in the market, we walk with our parents.
In church or mosque, we use a quiet voice.
Example: Do not run in the market or shout in worship places.
Class activity:
Let's practice walking in the market.
Line up and walk quietly without pushing.
Evaluation questions:
How should we behave in the market?
What voice should we use in worship places?
Why is it important to be good outside?
Summary:
Walk nicely and use your quiet voice in public.

topics.title: Solving little quarrels
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use words to solve problems.
The pupils should be able to ask for help when needed.
Introduction:
Sometimes friends argue over toys.
Today we will learn how to solve quarrels.
Content:
If someone takes your toy, say please give it back.\>Do not hit or push when you are angry.
Example: If you cannot solve it, tell the teacher.
Class activity:
Let's practice using words to solve problems.
I will act like I took your toy, what do you say?
Evaluation questions:
What should you use instead of hands?
When should you call a teacher?
Why is it good to use words?
Summary:
Use your words to solve problems and ask for help.

topics.title: Neatness and self care
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list two ways to stay neat.
The pupils should be able to care for their bodies.
Introduction:\>Last week we learned about solving quarrels.
Today we will learn about keeping ourselves clean.
Content:
Brush your teeth in the morning and before bed.\>Comb your hair and trim your nails regularly.
Example: Wash your hands after playing outside.
Class activity:
Let's pretend to brush our teeth.
Take your toothbrush and brush up and down.
Evaluation questions:
How many times should we brush our teeth?
What should we do with our hair?
Why is it important to be clean?
Summary:
Brush your teeth and keep your body clean.

topics.title: Children's rights
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name children's rights.
The pupils should be able to ask for help when unsafe.
Introduction:
Every child has rights in Nigeria.
Today we will learn about these rights.
Content:
Every child has the right to food, love and school.
If someone hurts you, tell a trusted adult.
Example: If a stranger touches you, tell your teacher.
Class activity:
Let's say our rights together.
We have the right to learn and play safely.
Evaluation questions:
What rights do children have?
Who should you tell if you feel unsafe?
Why is it important to know your rights?
Summary:
All children deserve food, love and school.

topics.title: Revision and culture day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to greet in their culture.
The pupils should be able to recite manners rules.
Introduction:
Today we will revise what we learned this term.\>We will also celebrate our different cultures.
Content:
Dress in your cultural clothes and greet properly.\>Recite our manners rules like please and thank you.
Example: In Yoruba culture, we greet with Eku ire.
Class activity:
Let's greet in different languages.
Who can greet in Igbo, Hausa or Yoruba?
Evaluation questions:
How do you greet in your language?
What is one manners rule you remember?
Why is it good to learn about cultures?
Summary:
Learn to greet in different languages and be polite.
